reason: Two activities with one identifier, one with a startTime and one with an endTime, unify into one record whose PROV-N text is the activity with both times and both extra attributes (PROV-CONSTRAINTS section 6.1, Constraint 22, #253). It took over `test_unification_rules.py::test_spec_worked_example_merges`, because its exact PROV-N text carries both times and both extra attributes that `_unify_same_type_group` merges for `ProvBundle._unified_records`, and the datetime object against string input difference ends in `_ensure_datetime`, which `ProvBundle.activity` applies before the record exists. The verifier planted a fault that took extra attributes from the first record only and a fault that took formal values from the first record only, and each failed this test. A third, fault 1c (`ProvBundle._unified_records` unifying only groups whose identifier has the empty prefix, so `ex:a` is skipped), failed many rows of test_unification_constraints.py::test_unified_corpus_characterization. This test uses the default-namespace identifier "a", whose prefix is empty, so fault 1c leaves it alone. Without lxml, where the corpus rows skip, a probe that left this module out found fault 1c still failing 30 tests, among them test_model.py::test_unifying.

Two activities with one identifier and different startTimes make `ProvDocument.unified` raise ProvUnificationError whose message names the identifier, prov:startTime and both values (PROV-CONSTRAINTS Constraint 22, #253). It was proposed as the takeover of `test_unification_rules.py::test_conflicting_concrete_formal_attributes_raise` and does not cover the qualified identifier in the message, because it uses a default-namespace identifier and asserts only its local part, so that test stayed. The verifier planted two faults in the message built by `_unify_same_type_group`, one that writes the local part and one that writes the IRI of the identifier, and each failed only that test.

The vendored ProvToolbox corpus holds 153 XML files, and every file the module names as a parse failure, a rejection or a party skip is one of them. The corpus README states the corpus holds 153 files, and the module tables must name real files (#253, #547, #710).

Records with one identifier in the top level, in one bundle twice and in another bundle once unify only inside their own scope, and the label values of each stay separate. PROV-CONSTRAINTS section 7.2 scopes unification to each bundle, and docs/explanation/unification-flattening.md says nothing merges across a bundle boundary.

An entity and an activity with one default-namespace identifier raise ProvUnificationError whose message names that identifier. PROV-CONSTRAINTS Constraint 55 (entity-activity-disjoint) in the scope of #253.

After `flattened()`, `unified()` merges records with one identifier from the top level and from two bundles into one record with all three labels. docs/explanation/unification-flattening.md describes `flattened().unified()` as a deliberate tool that merges across former bundle boundaries.

Each vendored PROV-XML file either makes `ProvDocument.unified` raise ProvUnificationError with the fragment its table gives, or unifies to the count of distinct identified records plus distinct anonymous ones (PROV-CONSTRAINTS Constraints 22 and 23 against the vendored ProvToolbox corpus, #253, the non-expandable rule of #547 and the party skips of #710). It has one row for each file, and the files differ in record kind and in which attribute conflicts, so no row is a drop. Its `generation-fail2` row took over `test_unification_rules.py::test_conflicting_relation_endpoints_raise`, because it raises from the same statement in `_unify_same_type_group`, reached through `ProvBundle._unified_records` and `_unify_record_group`, for the same cause, and also matches the message `has conflicting values`. The verifier planted a fault that skipped the conflict check for a value that is a QualifiedName, and 20 tests failed it, among them that row. Its `generation-fail1` row took over `test_unification_constraints.py::test_uniqueness_constraints_on_other_keys_are_out_of_scope`, because it reads the same four records (one entity, one activity and two generations of that pair under different identifiers) and asserts the count of 4 that `_expected_unified_count` derives, so it fails when `ProvBundle._unified_records` merges or rejects the two generations. The verifier planted a fault that merged the two generations and a fault that raised for them, and the row failed each. The rows skip without lxml, which every CI job that runs them installs, and `test_model.py::test_unifying` still guards the `generation-fail2` shape then.

Two generations of one entity and activity under different identifiers both stay after `ProvDocument.unified`, which leaves four records and raises nothing. Constraints 24 to 29 sit outside `ProvDocument.unified` and belong to the validation of #62, which the module docstring and the conformance page state. The `generation-fail1` row of `test_unification_constraints.py::test_unified_corpus_characterization` takes over, because it reads the same four records from PROV-XML and asserts the count of 4 that `_expected_unified_count` derives, so it fails when `ProvBundle._unified_records` merges or rejects the two generations. The verifier planted a fault that merged generations of one pair in `ProvBundle._unified_records` and a fault that raised for a repeated pair, and the row failed both. The mutation check over the records.py and bundle.py mutants found none that became undetected without this test. #253 names `generation-fail1` as the instance of Constraints 24 to 29 that `ProvDocument.unified` leaves alone. The row skips without lxml, which every CI job that runs it installs. The takeover row depends on `generation-fail1` staying out of every table in the module and on the vendored file `generation-fail1.xml`, which the register check does not follow.

The vendored W3C type corpus holds seven files, none of them in the ProvToolbox glob, and every file is a raise, an out-of-scope case or a pass case. The corpus README lists the seven W3C files, and the tables must stay in step with them (#253).

Each W3C type file makes `unified()` raise "incompatible types" for entity with activity, entity with generation and generation with usage, and does not raise for the other four. PROV-CONSTRAINTS Constraints 53, 54 and 55 as the W3C cases probe them (#253). Constraints 50 and 56 are not implemented, and validation beyond `unified()` is #62 on the conformance page.
